Imagine a Formula One car landing on your head.
At Monza in 2021, Max Verstappen's car landed on top of his.
Between his head and the tyre was a curved bar called the halo.
When it arrived in 2018, fans called it ugly, and some drivers agreed.
Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said, "If you give me a chainsaw, I would take it off."
But it's built to hold about twelve tonnes: a double-decker bus.
In Bahrain in 2020, Romain Grosjean hit a steel barrier at nearly two hundred kilometres an hour.
His car split in two and burst into flames.
The halo shielded his head as the car tore through the steel.
Nearly half a minute later, he climbed out of the fire.
Grosjean had doubted it. Now he called it the greatest thing F1 had brought in.
Back at Monza, Verstappen's rear tyre hit Hamilton's helmet, and the halo pushed it off.
Hamilton said it saved his neck. His team boss said it had definitely saved his life.
So next time you call it ugly, just...
